course_name_en: Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering I Engineering 1

learning_outcomes.text: Students can calculate electrical quantities in any network, select suitable measurement circuits for their measurement, and interpret, compare, and check the plausibility of the results.

They develop an understanding of the fundamental properties of the electric field and the functioning of capacitors and can calculate the associated quantities taking into account geometry and material and check the plausibility of the results.

Similarly, students know the basic properties of the magnetic field and the functioning of inductors and can calculate the associated quantities taking into account geometry and material and check the plausibility of the results.
Students differentiate between stationary, transient, and harmonic cases and can select and apply appropriate methods and calculation rules.
Through accompanying tutorials, technical competencies are consolidated, and social competencies (including teamwork) are conveyed through small group work.

After completing the internship, students are able to build simple electrical circuits and carry out and evaluate measurements with common measuring devices (multimeter, oscilloscope). The tasks are handled in small groups and defended in a post-colloquium. The knowledge learned from the lecture 'Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering I' will be applied and further problems can be solved with its help.
Through group work during the experiment execution and evaluation, teamwork as a formative social competence is strengthened.

syllabus_topics: Basic laws of the DC circuit (simple circuit, calculation of resistance networks)
Electric field (distinction from flow field, quantities for field description, behavior of capacitances in the circuit, application of the electric field)

Magnetic field (introduction, overview, quantities for field description, examples of magnetic fields, matter in the magnetic field, induction law, forces and energy in the magnetic field, comparison of E- and M-fields)
Basic laws of the AC circuit (introduction, phasor representation of sinusoidal quantities, simple sinusoidal circuit, complex sinusoidal circuit calculation, resonant circuits)
Experiment 1: Measurements in the DC circuit
assessment_rules: The 'Grundlagen der Elektrotechnik I' (Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering I) component is graded based on a written exam and accounts for 100% of the module grade. The 'Praktikum zu Grundlagen der Elektrotechnik I' (Laboratory to Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering I) component is ungraded and does not contribute to the module grade, requiring a pre-testat, practical experiment, protocol, and post-colloquium.
